newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit stays rangebound, seen rising on dlr sales.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit stays rangebound, seen rising on dlr sales.

text.p: The ringgit was rangebound in late Asian trading, but was expected to gain further if funds unloaded their long dollar positions, dealers said on Thursday.
They said the ringgit traded in the 2.5040/80 range for most of the day, with the pressure to sell curbed by fear of Bank Negara's intervention beyond 2.51 a dollar level.
Bank Negara on Wednesday intervened in the market to sell $100-200 million to help slow down the ringgit's fall.
"The ringgit is in a range, it is unlikely to come out overnight unless funds start selling their long dollars," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He said many market players were squaring off their positions close to the 2.5080 level. "After Negara's intervention, nobody wants to go in and test 2.51."
Dealers said they expected some funds to sell their long dollar positions in the near future, which could cause dollar/ringgit to test 2.50 to a dollar on Friday.
"People in London too are more inclined to sell dollars. This may take the ringgit down to 2.5030," one dealer said.
At 0900 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5040/50 a dollar and 1.7409/29 against the Singapore dollar.
